ai.description: *Hemidactylus hemchandrai* reaches 50 mm SVL. It is pale brown with dark dorsal crossbands. Key features include a strongly tuberculate dorsum and a tail with enlarged, pointed, whorled scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus hemchandrai* is best distinguished by the presence of 8–10 longitudinal rows of strongly keeled, trihedral tubercles on its dorsum, which are significantly larger than the surrounding granular scales.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus hemchandrai* is endemic to the rocky outcrops and scrub forests of the Northern Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Hemidactylus hemchandrai* is primarily nocturnal, emerging after sunset to actively hunt for small insects and arthropods on rocky surfaces and tree trunks.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus hemchandrai* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus hemchandrai* is endemic to the Western Ghats of Maharashtra, India, typically inhabiting rocky outcrops at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
